column1: # argmax-margin-floors.tsv: the calibrated floor of each argmax margin gate cell.
# One row per (model, prompt, decode program, device). The floor is the largest gap shift at an
# agreeing row, measured by `tools/argmax-margin-gate.sh <model> [--decode batch] --calibrate`
# over every row of the prompt (memra#1199, docs/decisions/ARGMAX-GATE-GAP-SHIFT-FLOOR.md).
# `rows` is the number of agreeing rows the floor is the maximum of and `set_by_row` the row
# that set it. `p50`, `p99` and `p999` are the median, 99th and 99.9th percentile of those
# rows' gap shift (nearest rank): a floor far above them was set by one or two rows.
# `prompt_sha256` binds the row to the prompt's bytes. `device` is the name nvidia-smi reports.
# `receipt` is the banked calibration log, the full per-row table.
# `known_rows` lists the calibration table's own flips whose gap shift is above the floor, as
# `row:prefill_top1:margin_p:decode_top1:margin_d` joined by `;` (`-` for none). These are rows
# where main's two programs already disagree by more than at any agreeing row of the prompt
# (memra#1203 asks which program is right there). A known row inside a judged window is
# printed and named, and does not fail the cell by itself. A candidate whose gap shift at a
# known row exceeds main's recorded shift at that row fails. A tighter guard, the candidate's
# rows against main's stored rows at the same positions, is memra#1204.
# Every field of the key must match exactly. There is no fallback row: a cell without one is
# UNCALIBRATED (a flip fails, agreeing rows are not judged, the release battery refuses).
# A row changes only by recalibration, in the PR whose decision record accepts the change of
# numeric class, with the old and the new row shown (docs/TESTING.md).
